candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort: assess skin/wounds, provide wound care, monitor comfort/pain and document findings needed to evaluate basic-care interventions.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — wound assessment and documentation
candidate.educational_objective: Document a wound comprehensively at baseline using precise location, measurements, wound-bed/periwound characteristics, drainage, pain and other relevant findings so later assessments can be compared accurately.

options.A: Record the wound stage and a photograph only; measurements and drainage characteristics can be added at discharge.
options.B: Record the dressing type and pain score only because wound-bed and surrounding-skin findings are treatment rather than assessment data.
options.C: Delay the baseline description until the first scheduled dressing change so admission findings do not affect later comparisons.
options.D: Record the wound's precise location, size, wound-bed and periwound findings, drainage characteristics, pain, and other relevant assessment findings.

candidate.rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills states that wound assessment and documentation should include the anatomic location, wound type and degree of tissue damage, wound bed, wound size, wound edges and periwound skin, signs of infection, pain, and drainage characteristics. Wounds should be measured on admission and at subsequent dressing changes so progress can be compared over time. Therefore D is correct. A omits key baseline measurements and drainage findings, B incorrectly excludes wound-bed/periwound assessment, and C delays information needed for comparison and care planning.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Comprehensive baseline wound documentation should include precise location, dimensions, wound-bed/periwound findings, drainage, pain and other relevant assessment characteristics, with measurements beginning on admission for later comparison.
candidate.source_locator: 20.3 Assessing Wounds: assessment/documentation includes anatomic location, wound type, tissue damage, wound bed, size, edges/periwound skin, signs of infection and pain. Type and Amount of Exudate: document color, consistency and amount. Wound Size: measure on admission and every dressing change. Checklist for Wound Assessment repeats location, dimensions, drainage, periwound, pain and infection findings.
